mainTopic: The widow's נדר for collecting her כתובה: רב הונא and רב נחמן on a remarried widow, and whether a vow must be spelled out to a חכם
overview: The amud opens at the end of a proof from a court letter. In that letter, a woman collected her כתובה by taking a נדר, and the proof was that a divorcée can do this too. רב אשי pushes the proof away: she got her גט from her יבם, so she collected from a dead husband's estate, like any widow. The גמרא then returns to רבן גמליאל הזקן's enactment that a widow takes a נדר for the יתומים. רב הונא limits it to a widow who has not remarried. He explains that a husband cannot cancel vows made before the marriage, and a חכם will not release this נדר, because the vow must be spelled out to him. רב נחמן disagrees and says even a remarried widow vows, because the court has her vow in public, and a public vow cannot be cancelled. Two ברייתות are brought against רב הונא, and the גמרא ends up saying the two sides follow a dispute between תנאים about public vows. Finally, רב נחמן and רב פפא argue about whether a person must spell out his vow to a חכם. A challenge to רב נחמן from a כהן who vowed to leave forbidden wives is left for the next amud.

steps.title: The end of the court letter used as a proof
steps.stepSummary: The quoted court letter ends: the property was valued at five מנה, and the court in בבל should collect the rest of her כתובה for her.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And we valued the property at five מנה. When she comes to you, collect the rest for her."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a quote from a court letter, brought as proof that a woman collected her כתובה after taking only a נדר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The letter describes a woman who was divorced and collected part of her כתובה after a נדר, not a שבועה. The court then told another court to collect the rest of the money for her. The proof is that a divorcée, and not only a widow, can collect with a נדר.

keyTerms.meaning: We valued them (we appraised the property)

phrases.english: And we appraised them at five maneh;
phrases.notes: A מנה is 100 דינרים, so this is 500 דינרים worth of property.

phrases.english: when she comes to you
phrases.notes: Literally "to your hands." The letter is written to a different court.

phrases.english: collect the rest for her."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the court letter that the previous part of the daf began quoting as a proof.
steps.raayaObject: That a divorcée can collect her כתובה with a נדר instead of a שבועה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A real court letter describing a woman who collected after a נדר.

steps.title: רב אשי says that woman had a divorce from her יבם
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי rejects the proof. The woman in the letter got a גט from her יבם, so she was really collecting as a widow.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: That divorce was a גט from a יבם.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי pushes away the proof from the letter by explaining that the woman in it was not an ordinary divorcée.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman who receives a גט from her יבם collects her כתובה from her first husband, who died. So she is collecting from a dead man's property, just like any widow. That is why a נדר was enough for her, and the letter proves nothing about a regular divorcée.

keyTerms.meaning: A divorce given by the יבם (the brother of the dead husband)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב אשי is saying the woman was not divorced. She did get a גט. He means her כתובה came from her dead first husband, so she collected the way a widow does.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
That one was a levirate divorce.
phrases.notes: He means she got the גט from her dead husband's brother, so she was collecting from the dead husband's estate.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: הָהוּא, גֵּט יְבָמִין הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought from the court letter.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof completely by reading the case differently. It does not say what the halacha is for a regular divorcée.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The woman in the letter was not a regular divorcée. She was collecting from a dead husband's estate, the way a widow does.

steps.title: רב הונא limits the נדר to a widow who has not remarried
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about רבן גמליאל's enactment. רב הונא says it applies only to a widow who has not remarried. A remarried widow is not given this נדר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: רבן גמליאל הזקן instituted that she should take a נדר. רב הונא said: This was taught only when she has not remarried. If she has remarried, we do not have her take a נדר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה about the widow's נדר, and רב הונא adds an important limit to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The enactment let a widow collect from the יתומים by taking a נדר, which is easier than a שבועה. רב הונא says this easier path is only for a widow who is still unmarried. If she has remarried, the נדר is not used.

keyTerms.meaning: They taught this only in the case of
We make someone take a נדר

steps.whyThisMatters: This limit sets up the next two questions, which test why remarriage should matter.

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel the Elder instituted
that she should take a vow, etc.:
Rav Huna said,
they taught this only where she did not remarry,
but if she remarried, we do not have her vow.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִתְקִין רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הַזָּקֵן שֶׁתְּהֵא נוֹדֶרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by going back to the line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A remarried widow is not given the נדר. The enactment applies only to a widow who has not remarried.

steps.title: Why not worry about a future husband too?
steps.stepSummary: The reason a remarried widow gets no נדר is that her husband could cancel it. But an unmarried widow might also remarry later, and then her new husband could cancel it.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason for a remarried widow? Because her husband can cancel her נדר. But even when she is not remarried, once she marries, her husband will cancel it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב הונא's line between a remarried widow and an unmarried one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that she might take a false נדר, trusting that her husband will cancel it with הפרה. If that is the worry, it should apply to an unmarried widow too, since she may marry later. So why should remarriage make a difference?

phrases.english: If she remarried, what is the reason?
Because the husband will annul it for her;
when she did not remarry, also,
when she marries, the husband will annul it for her!

steps.triggerLanguage: נִיסֵּת מַאי טַעְמָא – דְּמֵיפַר לַהּ בַּעַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reasoning behind רב הונא's limit.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's line between a remarried widow and an unmarried widow.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the worry is that a husband's הפרה will cancel the נדר, a future husband could do that too. So the unmarried widow should also be left out.

steps.title: A husband cannot cancel vows made before the marriage
steps.stepSummary: A husband cannot cancel a נדר his wife made before they married. So an unmarried widow's נדר is safe from a future husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: A husband does not cancel earlier vows.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a future husband cannot cancel this נדר, because she made it before marrying him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A husband's power of הפרה covers only vows his wife makes while married to him. A נדר she made while single stays in force. So only an already-married widow is a worry, and רב הונא's line holds.

keyTerms.meaning: Earlier ones, here vows made before the marriage

phrases.english: The husband does not annul earlier vows.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings in a general halacha about הפרה that removes the worry.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any husband she ever marries could cancel her נדר.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only vows made during the marriage can be cancelled by the husband. Vows from before the marriage cannot.

steps.title: Why not worry that a חכם will release her?
steps.stepSummary: Even without a husband, she could go to a חכם and have the נדר released. So why trust a נדר at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us worry that perhaps she will go to a חכם and he will release it for her!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new worry: a חכם can release any נדר, so the נדר might not stop her from lying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if no husband can cancel the נדר, there is still התרה, a release from a חכם. A widow who already got paid might take the נדר anyway, expecting a חכם to release it later. That would make the whole enactment weak.

keyTerms.meaning: A Torah scholar who can release a נדר

phrases.english: But let us be concerned that perhaps she will go to a sage
and he will release it for her!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנֵיחוּשׁ דִּלְמָא אָזְלָה לְגַבֵּי חָכָם וְשָׁרֵי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the husband worry is answered, the גמרא raises a second way the נדר could be undone.
steps.kashyaTarget: Relying on a נדר at all, even for an unmarried widow.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A חכם's התרה could undo the נדר, so she might vow falsely, expecting to be released later.

steps.title: A person must spell out the נדר to the חכם
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא holds that someone asking for התרה must describe the נדר in detail. A חכם who hears it was a כתובה vow will not release it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that one must spell out the details of the נדר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב הונא holds you must tell the חכם exactly what the נדר was. That ends the worry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she must tell the חכם exactly what the נדר was, he will know it was taken so she could collect her כתובה. He will not release a נדר like that. So the נדר stays reliable, and only a husband's הפרה, which needs no explanation, is a real worry.

keyTerms.meaning: To spell out the details of the נדר

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא: the court gives the נדר only to a widow who has not remarried. A future husband cannot cancel vows made before the marriage, and a חכם will not release this נדר, because she must tell him what it was.

phrases.english: He holds that one must detail the vow.
phrases.notes: "He" is רב הונא. Once the חכם hears the details, he won't release a vow taken to collect a כתובה.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to רב הונא's view on how התרה works.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: She could quietly have a חכם release the נדר.
steps.terutzMaskana: She must spell out the נדר to the חכם, so he will not release it.

steps.title: רב נחמן: even a remarried widow takes the vow
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן disagrees with רב הונא and says even a remarried widow is given the vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: Even if she remarried, she takes the vow and collects.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא, רב נחמן, disagrees with רב הונא. He says the vow is given even to a widow who already remarried.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא limited רבן גמליאל's enactment to a widow who has not remarried. רב נחמן says the enactment covers every widow, even one who remarried. The גמרא will now ask how that can work if her husband can cancel the vow.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
Even if she remarried.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents an opposing view to רב הונא's ruling in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a remarried widow is given the vow and collects her כתובה.

steps.title: But her new husband will cancel the vow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב נחמן: a remarried widow's husband can simply cancel her vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she remarried, her husband will surely cancel the vow for her!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב נחמן. If she is married, her husband can cancel her vow, so the vow is worthless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same reason רב הונא gave for excluding a remarried widow. A vow made while married falls under the husband's power of הפרה. So how can רב נחמן trust such a vow?

keyTerms.meaning: A husband's cancelling of his wife's vow

phrases.english: If she remarried, the husband will certainly cancel it for her!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב נחמן's ruling from step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling that a remarried widow takes the vow
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A husband can cancel a vow his wife makes during the marriage, so the vow gives the orphans no protection.

steps.title: The vow is taken in public
steps.stepSummary: The court has her vow in public, and a husband cannot cancel a public vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: We have her vow in public, so the husband cannot cancel it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רב נחמן. The court has her take the vow in front of many people, and that kind of vow cannot be cancelled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן holds that a נדר made ברבים is beyond a husband's הפרה. So the problem from step 9 disappears, and the vow protects the orphans even after she remarries.

keyTerms.meaning: In public, in front of many people

phrases.english: Because we have her vow in public.
phrases.notes: The idea assumed here is that a husband cannot cancel a vow made in public.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Adds a new legal principle: a public vow cannot be cancelled
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A husband can cancel any vow his wife makes while married.
steps.terutzMaskana: A vow the court makes her take in public is beyond his power to cancel.

steps.title: A ברייתא implies a remarried widow vows
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a remarried widow collects if she vowed, which seems to mean she vows now, against רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: If she remarried, she collects her כתובה if she vowed. Doesn't that mean she vows now?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge רב הונא. It reads the ברייתא as saying a widow can vow after remarrying and then collect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא said a remarried widow is not given the vow. The ברייתא says that a remarried widow collects "if she vowed." The simple reading is that she vows now, after remarrying, which is exactly what רב הונא rejected.

phrases.english: They raised an objection: If she remarried,
she collects her כתובה if she vowed.
What, is it not that she vows now?
phrases.notes: "Now" means after she has already remarried.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: נִיסֵּת – גּוֹבָה כְּתוּבָּתָהּ אִם נָדְרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רב הונא's position and attacks it with a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling that a remarried widow is not given the vow
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lets a remarried widow collect through a vow, which seems to mean a vow taken after remarriage.

steps.title: She vowed before remarrying
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא means she vowed earlier, before she remarried.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it means she vowed at the start, before remarrying.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב הונא. It rereads the ברייתא as a case where she took the vow before her new marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Based on step 5, a vow made before marriage is safe from the husband. So the ברייתא only says that a widow who already vowed can still collect after remarrying. This fits רב הונא.

phrases.english: No, where she vowed at the outset.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the ברייתא (the vow was made earlier)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא means she vowed after remarrying.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא means she vowed before remarrying, so it fits רב הונא.

steps.title: A clearer ברייתא: she vows after remarrying
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא says plainly that a remarried widow vows and collects.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught: If she remarried, she vows and collects her כתובה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא against רב הונא. This one clearly says she vows after remarrying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the wording is "she vows and collects," in the present. It cannot be reread as a vow made earlier. So רב הונא seems directly contradicted.

phrases.english: But it was taught: If she remarried,
she vows and collects her כתובה!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A stronger challenge that the answer of step 12 cannot handle.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא explicitly has the remarried widow vowing now, which cannot be explained as an earlier vow.

steps.title: A dispute between תנאים about public vows
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתות reflect a dispute between תנאים over whether a husband can cancel a public vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a dispute between תנאים. One says a vow made in public can be cancelled. Another says it cannot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this ברייתא follows a different תנא. רב הונא follows the תנא on the other side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everything depends on whether a husband can cancel a public vow. The opinion that he can matches רב הונא, so a remarried widow cannot vow. The opinion that he cannot matches the ברייתא and רב נחמן's answer in step 10.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute between תנאים

steps.whatToRemember: The whole argument between רב הונא and רב נחמן depends on one question: can a husband cancel a vow made in public? רב הונא says yes, and רב נחמן says no. Each side has a תנא to rely on.

phrases.english: It is a dispute of תנאים,
for there is one who says:
A vow made in public
can be cancelled;
and there is one who says:
it cannot be cancelled.

steps.terutzResolutionType: The sources reflect a dispute between תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is the final word against רב הונא.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב הונא follows a different תנא, who holds that a public vow can be cancelled.

steps.title: Must a person spell out the vow for התרה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether someone requesting התרה must describe the vow in detail.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: Does a person need to spell out the vow, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question that grows out of step 7. Does someone asking a חכם to release a vow have to explain exactly what the vow was?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's answer in step 7 assumed that a person must give the details. Now the גמרא asks whether that is actually the rule. The answer is about to come as a dispute.

phrases.english: It was asked of them:
Does one need to spell out the vow,
phrases.notes: This is about a person asking a חכם to release his vow.

phrases.english: or does he not need to?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: צָרִיךְ לְפָרֵט אֶת הַנֶּדֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a side question based on the assumption in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a person asking for התרה must describe his vow in detail.

steps.title: רב נחמן says no, רב פפא says yes
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says there is no need to spell out the vow. רב פפא says there is.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: He does not need to. רב פפא said: He needs to.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the question, and they disagree. רב נחמן says no details are needed, and רב פפא says they are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא's view matches what רב הונא assumed in step 7. רב נחמן's view means the חכם does not have to hear what the vow was about.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: He does not need to;
Rav Pappa said: He needs to.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the answers to the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A dispute: רב נחמן says no details are required, and רב פפא says details are required.

steps.title: Why רב נחמן says no details are needed
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן explains that requiring details is risky. The person might shorten his description, the חכם would release only what he heard, and the person would wrongly think the whole vow is gone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן says he does not need to spell out the vow. If you require it, sometimes the person will cut his description short, and the חכם releases only what he heard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats רב נחמן's view from step 16, and this time it adds his reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the person must describe the vow, he may describe only part of it. The חכם can release only what was said to him, so the rest of the vow is still in force. The person, though, will act as if all of it is gone. It is safer for him to just say 'I made a vow' and have the חכם release the whole thing.

keyTerms.meaning: A Torah scholar who has the power to release vows

phrases.english: Rav Nachman says: he does not need to
for if you say he needs to,
sometimes he will cut his statement short,
and the sage dissolves only what he hears.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ – דְּאִי אָמְרַתְּ צָרִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats רב נחמן's ruling from step 16 and adds the reason behind it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is no need to spell out the vow, because a partial description leads to only a partial release.

steps.title: Why רב פפא says details are needed
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that the vow may have been made to keep someone away from something forbidden. The חכם must know this so he does not release it by mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא says he does need to spell out the vow, because it might involve a matter of prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רב פפא's reason for requiring the person to describe the vow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some vows exist to protect against a sin. One example is the widow's vow in our משנה, which keeps her from lying. If the חכם does not know what the vow is for, he might release a vow that should never be released.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa says: he needs to
because of a matter of prohibition.
phrases.notes: The vow might be there to keep someone from doing something forbidden, so the sage has to know what it is.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר צָרִיךְ – מִשּׁוּם מִילְּתָא דְּאִיסּוּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing reason, for רב פפא's side of the dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The vow must be spelled out, so that a vow guarding against a prohibition is not released by mistake.

steps.title: A challenge from the priest who married forbidden women
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says a כהן who married forbidden women may not serve until he vows not to benefit from them. A ברייתא adds that he may serve right after vowing and divorce them afterward. If no details are needed for התרה, we should worry that he will get the vow quietly released.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה: one who marries women in sin is disqualified until he vows not to benefit from them. A ברייתא taught about this: he vows and serves, then goes down and divorces. If you say he does not need to spell out the vow, we should worry that he might go to a חכם and have it released!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה and a ברייתא to challenge רב נחמן's view that a vow does not need to be spelled out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא trusts the כהן's vow so fully that he may serve in the מקדש before he has actually divorced. That makes sense only if he cannot easily undo the vow. Under רב נחמן, he could just tell a חכם 'I made a vow' and get it released without the חכם knowing it was about forbidden wives. The ברייתא shows no such worry, which suggests the vow must be spelled out, as רב פפא says.

keyTerms.meaning: That he vows not to benefit (from them)
To spell out the details of the vow

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a real test case. Here the vow exists to keep someone away from a prohibition, which is exactly the kind of case רב פפא worried about.

phrases.english: We learned in a mishna:
One who marries women in transgression is disqualified,
phrases.notes: This is a כהן who married women forbidden to him. He may not serve in the מקדש.

phrases.english: until he vows not to benefit from them.
And it was taught about this:
He vows and serves,
then goes down and divorces.
phrases.notes: He goes down from his Temple service and only then divorces his wives.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ לְפָרֵט אֶת הַנֶּדֶר,
phrases.english: And if you say he does not need to spell out the vow,
let us worry that perhaps he will go to a sage
and he will release it for him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the dispute from steps 17 and 18 against a known משנה and ברייתא, and challenges רב נחמן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's view that a person asking for התרה does not need to spell out the vow.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lets the כהן serve right after vowing, so it must not fear that he will undo the vow. Under רב נחמן, he could easily get it released without revealing what it was about, so the ברייתא should have been worried.
